# Data Integration
## Loading Adjusted Market Data

```{python}
#| label: load_data
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.dates as mdates

# Pointing to the time-adjusted output from your python script
df_combined = pd.read_csv("data/final_adjusted.csv")

# Ensure Sold Date is datetime for plotting
df_combined["Sold Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df_combined["Sold Date"])

# Define the target lien date for the visual label
lien_date = pd.Timestamp("2026-01-01")

print(f"Total Adjusted Sales Loaded: {len(df_combined)}")
print(f"Segments available: {df_combined['segment'].unique()}")
```

## Price Adustment Visual

```{python}
# | label: trend_visualization_refined
# | code-fold: true

# Use the standardized SqFt column from the clean script
sqft_col = "TotGLA" if "TotGLA" in df_combined.columns else "Total SqFt"

# Filter for Residential visualization (ensure valid SqFt and positive prices)
df_plot = df_combined[
    (df_combined["segment"] == "Residential") & (df_combined[sqft_col] > 100)
].copy()

# Unit Price Calculation
# 'Adj_Price' is the original sale minus concessions
# 'Trended_Price' is that value brought forward to 2026
df_plot["Price_SqFt_Original"] = df_plot["Adj_Price"] / df_plot[sqft_col]
df_plot["Price_SqFt_Trended"] = df_plot["Trended_Price"] / df_plot[sqft_col]

# Statistical Cleaning for Plotting (98th percentile to remove outliers)
y_limit = df_plot["Price_SqFt_Original"].quantile(0.98)
df_plot = df_plot[df_plot["Price_SqFt_Original"] < y_limit]
df_plot["date_num"] = mdates.date2num(df_plot["Sold Date"])

plt.figure(figsize=(16, 8))

# Volatile Original Market (Lowess curve for localized trends)
sns.regplot(
    data=df_plot,
    x="date_num",
    y="Price_SqFt_Original",
    scatter_kws={"alpha": 0.1, "color": "gray", "s": 12},
    line_kws={
        "color": "#e74c3c",
        "label": "Original Market (Historical)",
        "linewidth": 3,
    },
    lowess=True,
)

# Stabilized Trended Market
sns.regplot(
    data=df_plot,
    x="date_num",
    y="Price_SqFt_Trended",
    scatter=False,
    line_kws={
        "color": "#3498db",
        "label": f"Trended/Stabilized to {lien_date.date()}",
        "linewidth": 4,
    },
    lowess=False,
)

# Formatting
ax = plt.gca()
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b %Y"))
plt.ylim(0, y_limit)
plt.title("Residential Housing Market Stabilization", fontsize=22, pad=20)
plt.xlabel("Sale Date", fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel("Price per Square Foot ($)", fontsize=14)
plt.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=13)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Sample MLR

```{python}
# | label: auto_MLR_no_leakage
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import numpy as np

# Updated list to include the "Cheating" variables
cols_to_remove = [
    "Time_1",
    "Time_2",
    "Time_3",
    "Time_4",
    "Time_5",
    "Sold Date",
    "Concessions Amount",
    "segment",
    "Age",
    "Sold Price",
    "ln_Price",
    "ln_GLA", 
    "Adj_Price"
]

df_mlr = (
    df_combined[df_combined["segment"] == "Residential"]
    .drop(columns=[c for c in cols_to_remove if c in df_combined.columns])
    .copy()
)

# Prune columns that are mostly empty
threshold = len(df_mlr) * 0.5
killer_cols = df_mlr.columns[df_mlr.count() < threshold].tolist()
df_mlr = df_mlr.drop(columns=killer_cols)

df_mlr = df_mlr.dropna()

if not df_mlr.empty:
    target = "Trended_Price"
    features = []

    for col in df_mlr.columns:
        if col == target:
            continue

        if col == "NbhdCode2":
            if df_mlr[col].nunique() > 1:
                features.append("C(NbhdCode2)")
        elif col in ["TotGLA", "Total SqFt"]:
            features.append(f"np.log(Q('{col}'))")
        elif np.issubdtype(df_mlr[col].dtype, np.number):
            if df_mlr[col].std() > 0:
                features.append(f"Q('{col}')")

    formula = f"np.log({target}) ~ {' + '.join(features)}"

    try:
        model = smf.ols(formula, data=df_mlr).fit()
        print(model.summary())
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Model failed: {e}")
```

## Diagnostic Plots

```{python}
# | label: diagnostic_plots
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Use the residuals and fitted values from your 'model'
residuals = model.resid
fitted = model.fittedvalues

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 10))

# Residuals vs Fitted (Corrected: y should be residuals)
sns.residplot(
    x=fitted,
    y=residuals,
    lowess=True,
    ax=axes[0, 0],
    line_kws={"color": "red", "lw": 1},
)
axes[0, 0].set_title("Residuals vs Fitted")
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel("Fitted values")
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("Residuals")

# Normal Q-Q
sm.qqplot(residuals, line="45", fit=True, ax=axes[0, 1])
axes[0, 1].set_title("Normal Q-Q")

# Scale-Location
sns.scatterplot(x=fitted, y=np.sqrt(np.abs(residuals)), ax=axes[1, 0])
axes[1, 0].set_title("Scale-Location")
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel("Fitted values")
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("sqrt(abs(Residuals))")

# Residuals vs Leverage
sm.graphics.influence_plot(model, criterion="cooks", ax=axes[1, 1])
axes[1, 1].set_title("Residuals vs Leverage")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
